title: A weekly visit
hook: visiting family or the sick weekly
tomorrow: why would three nights in the middle of a month be 'white'?

segments.voice: Yesterday, every week: the circle where the settling happens. This week also gave you a Friday washed and scented, a light, a hidden hour, blessings counted on the fingers, and two fast days. One weekly habit left: a visit.
screen: `EVERY WEEK.` → `THE WHOLE WEEK, BACK.` → `ONE HABIT LEFT.`

segments.voice: A hospital room: a chair nobody sits in for long, a TV on mute, a tray of food going cold. You brought flowers, you said hello, and now the quiet is getting long and you have no idea what to say next. The reports give an answer, and it's shorter than you'd guess.
screen: `A CHAIR, A MUTED TV.` → `NO IDEA WHAT TO SAY.` → `SHORTER THAN YOU'D GUESS.`

segments.voice: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ visits a sick man and says: no harm, it's a cleansing, if God wills. Short. Hopeful. No lecture. And the visit itself carries weight. In Sahih Muslim there's a hadith qudsi, where the Prophet reports God's words. On the Day of Resurrection, God says: son of Adam, I was sick and you didn't visit Me. The person answers: how could I visit You, the Lord of the worlds? And God says: didn't you know My servant so-and-so was sick? Had you visited him, you would have found Me with him. Here's the thing to tell someone tonight: God doesn't say you'd have found a reward beside that bed. He says you'd have found Him. Another report in the same collection says the visitor walks in the harvest of Paradise until they go home. And weekly matters too. Illness and loneliness don't keep a calendar, but a visitor who comes back every Saturday turns into someone a person can count on.
screen: `NO HARM: A CLEANSING.` · `I WAS SICK; YOU DIDN'T VISIT.` · `YOU'D HAVE FOUND ME WITH HIM.` · `SOMEONE TO COUNT ON.` · then, large: `EVERY WEEK, A VISIT.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one person who's sick, alone, or simply hard to visit. See the door you'd knock on and the chair you'd sit in. Choose the day this week you could go, or call, and hold that picture until the sit ends.
screen: `ONE PERSON.` · `THE DOOR, THE CHAIR.` · `ONE DAY THIS WEEK.`

segments.voice: A weekly visit: going to see the sick, or family, on a regular day, where, the report says, God is found with the one you visit.
Here's the line: every week, a visit, and a chair beside someone who's waiting. The weekly rhythm, seven of seven.

howItsDone: Muslims visit the sick at home or in the hospital, keeping visits short and hopeful, and some families keep a regular day for seeing grandparents and relatives.

pairs: his words to a sick man
someone a person can count on

myth: the Prophet's words to a sick man were long and full of advice
they were short: no harm, a cleansing, God willing.
in a report, God says: had you visited him, you'd have found Me with him
Sahih Muslim, a hadith qudsi, spoken by God on the Day of Resurrection.
visiting the sick only counts if they're family
the report says 'My servant so-and-so': anyone who is sick.

fork.setup: your friend's mom is home after surgery. you can visit once for two hours, or stop by for fifteen minutes every week. what fits today's lesson?
options: the short weekly visit: someone she can count on.
the one long visit: the length is what counts.
neither. a text is just the same as being there.
fork.reveal: the reports set no length, and his own words were short. a visit that comes back each week becomes something a sick person can lean on.

original.note: Arabic: 'iyada, visiting someone who is sick.

trapdoor: what you thought: visiting the sick is good manners.
what it means: a regular visit where, the report says, God is found with the one you visit.
what a scholar hears: Muslim 2569 is a hadith qudsi; Bukhari 5656 gives 'la ba's, tahur, in sha' Allah'; Muslim 2568 puts the visitor in the khurfa, the harvest, of Paradise.
guess: going regularly to see the sick, or family
a yearly trip to visit family graves
hosting guests at home every Friday night

chat.says: driving dadi to see khala samina after her hip surgery. every saturday now. what do i even SAY in there
options: keep it short and hopeful, like the Prophet: no harm, God willing. then just stay a while.
bring up her diagnosis and give advice. visiting is mostly about fixing the problem.
say nothing and let dadi talk. the visit really only counts for the one who's related.
chat.meaning: In Bukhari's report, the Prophet told a sick man: no harm, a cleansing, God willing. Short and hopeful; and the visit is where God is found.

hadith qudsi.meaning: a saying in which the Prophet reports God's words

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major collection of the Prophet's sayings

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 5656 (visiting a sick Bedouin: no harm, a purification, if God wills)
Sahih Muslim 2569 (hadith qudsi: 'son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me … you would have found Me with him')
Sahih Muslim 2568 (the visitor of the sick is in the harvest of Paradise until he returns)
